title: Traffic Contracts & Safety Sandbox for Incremental Model Admission
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a declarative "traffic contract" language and an isolated safety sandbox runtime to author, validate, and simulate incremental model admission policies. Goal: enable PMs/SEs to define traffic splits, step schedules, cohort constraints, shadow probes, and rollback predicates as first-class contracts that are enforced by the serving orchestration layer. The sandbox will let teams run deterministic simulations and lightweight canary dry-runs against anonymized telemetry so operators can validate safety rules before hitting production. Out of scope for this ticket: full RBAC UI integration and enterprise audit export (follow-up work).
acceptance_criteria: TCL parser implements traffic_split, step_schedule, shadow_probe, and rollback_predicate constructs and has unit tests covering edge cases
Safety sandbox runtime can ingest historical telemetry snapshot and run a policy simulation producing a timeline of traffic fractions and triggers
Serving runtime hook honors admitted traffic_contracts at rollout time and enforces realtime rollback predicate evaluation (latency and error-rate percentiles)
Console exposes a validation view with simulation timeline and a downloadable execution log
E2E test demonstrating a simulated canary that moves 0% -> 5% -> 25% then auto-rollback on 95th percentile latency breach
discussion: 2025-02-12 Maya Chen: Kickoff — defined scope and success metrics. Proposed a lightweight DSL (TCL) instead of full policy UI. Raised need for an anonymized telemetry snapshot format.

2025-02-17 Arjun Patel: Prototype TCL grammar in parser repo (link below). Initial grammar supports 'phase', 'fraction', 'duration', 'shadow_probe', 'predicate' clauses. Performance note: parsing step schedules should be O(n) to validate in dashboard.

2025-02-20 Design review (Luis): Suggested adding UX-friendly shorthand for common patterns (e.g., 'quick-smoke' macro) and a simulation 'what-if' slider in Console. Action: add macro layer to DSL for Console consumption.

2025-02-23 PM feedback (Rhea): Require that rollback predicates support percentile-based metrics (p50/p95/p99) and not just averages. Also require a 'grace' window to avoid noisy flips. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-02-26 Eng review (SRE - Priya): Raised an operational concern: realtime predicate evaluation must be bounded to avoid cold-path amplification. Decided to use streaming bucketing with fixed windowing (configurable) and fall back to approximate sketches for high-cardinality metrics.

2025-02-28 Arjun: Sandbox runner prototype completed. Ran simulation against anonymized prod snapshot from 2025-01-12. Found an edge case where shadow_probe traffic caused KV cache pressure in the runtime; mitigated by throttling shadow probe rate in runtime config.

2025-03-01 Maya: PR opened with TCL parser, simulator harness, and initial console validation UI (see links). Marked as In Progress; remaining: integration tests and SLA-based rollback hook in runtime.

Review notes: GitHub PR requests: expand unit tests for negative fractions, add more simulation scenarios (A/B vs canary), and include detailed runbook for operators explaining how to interpret simulation logs.
